overview: This chapter follows Renaissance planning and learning in Poland-Lithuania. Zamosc offers a local view of how architectural ideas, commerce and education could meet in one deliberately planned town.

items.text: The Union of Lublin joined the Polish Crown and Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the Commonwealth under one monarch in 1569.
In the late sixteenth century, Bernardo Morando designed Zamosc using Italian Renaissance ideas of an ideal city, adapted to Central European architectural traditions.
Zamosc was conceived as a trading centre on a route connecting western and northern Europe with the Black Sea. Arcaded merchants' houses enclosed its main market square.
Founder Jan Zamoyski established the Zamosc Academy. The planned town combined education with residential, commercial and civic functions.
